claims: Submitting Form 4868 by April 15 provides an automatic six-month extension until October 15 to file.
The extension is to file, not to pay taxes due.
IRS Free File allows electronic filing of Form 4868 for free regardless of income.

Paying all or part of estimated income tax due using Direct Pay, a debit/credit card, or the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) and selecting "Extension" as the reason results in the IRS automatically processing the extension without filing Form 4868.
Most tax software providers (e.g., TurboTax, H&R Block) offer free federal extension filing.
Paper Form 4868 must be postmarked by April 15.
Taxes owed must be paid by April 15 to avoid penalties.
Late filing penalties can be up to 5% of the unpaid tax per month.
Late payment penalties are generally 0.5% per month.
Late payment penalties have a maximum of 25%.
Victims of certain natural disasters may receive automatic extensions without filing Form 4868.
Automatic extensions for victims of certain natural disasters are listed on the IRS disaster relief page.
A federal extension does not automatically extend the state tax deadline.
